sentence: I am a student
hint: Subject + verb to be + article + noun
explanation: En inglés, el orden básico de la oración es Sujeto + Verbo + Objeto. 'I am a student' sigue este patrón.

sentence: She likes red apples
explanation: En inglés, el adjetivo 'red' va antes del sustantivo 'apples'.

sentence: The cat is on the table
hint: Subject + verb to be + preposition + place
explanation: 'The cat is on the table' usa 'is' (singular) porque hay un solo gato. 'Are' es para sujetos plurales.

sentence: We go to school every day
explanation: Las expresiones de tiempo como 'every day' van al final de la oración.

sentence: He has a big dog
explanation: Con 'He' se usa 'has', no 'have'. 'Have' se usa con I/you/we/they.

sentence: They are from Spain
hint: Subject + verb to be + preposition + country

sentence: I drink water every morning
hint: Use the base form of the verb with 'I'
explanation: Con 'I' se usa la forma base 'drink', no 'drinks'. 'Drinks' es para he/she/it.

sentence: My name is Maria
explanation: Esta es una forma común de presentarte en inglés.

sentence: Do you like coffee
hint: Questions start with an auxiliary verb

sentence: There are two books on the desk
explanation: Se usa 'there are' con sustantivos plurales como 'books'. 'There is' es para sustantivos singulares.

sentence: She is a good teacher
explanation: En inglés, los adjetivos van antes del sustantivo: 'good teacher', no 'teacher good'.

sentence: We live in a small house
explanation: 'Lives' es para he/she/it. Con 'we' se usa la forma base 'live'.

sentence: The children play in the park
explanation: 'Children' es plural, así que se usa 'play', no 'plays'.

sentence: He works at a hospital
explanation: Con 'he/she/it' se agrega -s al verbo: 'works', no 'work'.

sentence: She has three cats at home
explanation: Los números van antes de los sustantivos: 'three cats'. Se usa 'has' con he/she/it.

sentence: The book is under the chair
hint: Subject + be + preposition of place + location
explanation: Las preposiciones de lugar (under, on, in, next to) van entre el verbo y la ubicación.

sentence: My mother cooks dinner every night
explanation: 'My mother' es tercera persona del singular (she), así que se usa 'cooks' con -s.

sentence: They eat lunch at school
explanation: El patrón es: Sujeto + verbo + objeto + lugar.

sentence: It is very cold today
hint: We use 'it is' to talk about weather
explanation: En inglés, se usa 'it' como sujeto para hablar del clima: 'It is cold', no simplemente 'Is cold'.

sentence: She reads books in the library
explanation: Con 'she', el verbo necesita -s: 'reads'. 'Read' es para I/you/we/they.

sentence: There is a park near my house
explanation: 'Park' es singular, así que se usa 'there is'. 'There are' es para sustantivos plurales.

sentence: I always wake up at seven
hint: Adverbs of frequency go before the main verb
explanation: Los adverbios de frecuencia (always, usually, never) van antes del verbo principal: 'I always wake up'.

sentence: He is ten years old
hint: In English we use 'be' for age, not 'have'
explanation: El inglés usa 'is' para la edad: 'He is ten years old', a diferencia del español que usa 'tiene'.

sentence: The dog sleeps on the sofa
explanation: 'The dog' es singular (it), así que se usa 'sleeps' con -s.

sentence: We usually have breakfast at eight
hint: Adverb of frequency before the main verb
explanation: 'Usually' va antes del verbo principal 'have': 'We usually have breakfast'.

sentence: My sister works in a bank
explanation: 'My sister' es tercera persona del singular (she), así que se usa 'works' con -s.

sentence: Can you open the window
hint: Requests with 'can' start with the modal verb
explanation: Las preguntas con 'can' empiezan con el verbo modal: 'Can you...?'.

sentence: I never eat meat
hint: Adverbs of frequency go before the main verb
explanation: 'Never' va antes del verbo principal 'eat': 'I never eat meat'.

sentence: There are three chairs in the kitchen
explanation: 'Chairs' es plural, así que se usa 'there are', no 'there is'.

sentence: She doesn't like spiders
explanation: Con 'she' se usa 'doesn't' para negar, no 'don't'. 'Don't' es para I/you/we/they.
